items.context: r/HearingAids 板块, 我方身份=OTC助听器代工厂主(u/luogangan), 已发4篇工厂视角科普帖建立信誉 | 这是我上条回复邀请他讲经历后, 他给出的长篇自述
items.text: When I got my first pair of hearing aids about six years ago, they were way too sharp and loud. Fork on plate was like ice pick in the ear. I complained to that audiologist. But she said I'm only trying to get you back to normal. My mistake was not pushing harder. I ended up not wearing them for four years, until I figured out how to do the programming myself. Made do with the Apple AirPods and their hearing aid function. Then about six months ago, I decided to give hearing aids another try. Different audiologist, told her very firmly about my previous experience. I paid a premium to go to a clinic that did both earwax removal and real ear measurement. My current audiologist is exceptional. You could call it a three-way dance between the devices, her skill and judgment, and the feedback I give her. My level of intelligibility is vastly improved and I wear them all day every day. Audiologists talk about give your brain time to adjust. But when things are right, the adjustment is easy and painless. The problem is that that idea also covers the situations when things are just wrong. And it can be used to excuse a poor fitting.

items.context: r/HearingAids 板块, 我方身份=OTC助听器代工厂主(u/luogangan), 已发4篇工厂视角科普帖建立信誉 | 他引用我帖子里关于钱花在哪的段落, 提出定价结构质疑
items.text: "Same receiver suppliers, often the same chip families, so the raw components are less different than people assume. Where the money actually goes on a prescription device is the fitting software ecosystem, the clinical validation, the channel margin, and the service that comes with it." So why don't they charge the right amount for the aids, and more for the fitting?

items.context: r/HearingAids 板块, 我方身份=OTC助听器代工厂主(u/luogangan), 已发4篇工厂视角科普帖建立信誉 | 他在我的蓝牙帖下补充了一个自测出来的LE Audio通话缺陷
items.text: I've been working on an issue where people on phone calls can't hear me clearly. They say my voice is very quiet. I have Starkey Omega AI 24 mRICs, Google Pixel 10 Pro. The culprit is LE Audio. On a phone call with LE Audio enabled and using the mic on the phone, the phone's mic volume is lowered. I used an echo test phone number. With LE Audio enabled it was difficult to hear what I was saying. When I disabled it, which forces bluetooth classic, my voice was loud and clear. So while they work great for audio coming in, they kinda suck at actually using the phone. I'll be contacting the android Accessibility team. Also there's a tiny dongle, FlooGoo FMA120 on Amazon. It has the bluetooth radio needed for hearing aids with LE Audio. I have one. It works.

items.context: r/HearingAids 板块, 我方身份=OTC助听器代工厂主(u/luogangan), 已发4篇工厂视角科普帖建立信誉 | 我解释NFMI物理限制后, 他自己找到了变通办法
items.text: OK, I solved it, or rather, figured out a workaround. If my head is giving the low power signal some problems, what if I gave the signal an easier path? So if I am touching both HAs at the same time while pressing a button on either, it works flawlessly; a button press on one HA is registered on the other. My arms/body provide a seemingly easier conduit for the signal. Who woulda thunk?!
